approved: Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Amendment (Dairy Produce) Bill 2014

Supported the dairy levies bill raising the cap on Animal Health Australia levies without increasing the rate paid by farmers, but moved an amendment criticising the government for failing to urgently address drought and for omitting resource sustainability from its agriculture white paper terms of reference, saying $40 million had been withheld from Labor's $420 million Farm Finance package.

Supported the dairy levies bill, saying agriculture and food manufacturing employ around 2,000 and 4,000 people respectively in her Bendigo electorate, highlighting local producers including Symons Dairy, Jonesy's Dairy Fresh and Holy Goat Cheese, and called for urgent government action on drought affecting farmers further north.

Supported the dairy levies bill as a step toward future-proofing the industry, citing New Zealand's Fonterra cooperative, which accounts for more than 90 per cent of that country's dairy market, as a model for Australian dairy to pursue deregulation and Asian market access.

Supported the dairy levies bill, saying the carbon tax has cost dairy processing about $7,000 per supplying farm, citing Murray-Goulburn as an example, and criticised the market dominance of Coles and Woolworths over milk pricing, arguing export markets are the best way to free farmers from supermarket control.

Supported the dairy levies bill, noting Australia's dairy farmer numbers fell from around 22,000 in 1980 to just over 6,000 today, and warned that climate change poses growing risks to water, feed supply and disease management for the industry.

Supported the dairy levies bill, describing dairying as Tasmania's largest agricultural sector, with 1,500 people employed on farms producing about 770 million litres of milk a year, and said his Braddon electorate holds more than half of the state's dairy farms.

Supported the dairy levies bill and the opposition's drought amendment, citing a Queensland Dairyfarmers' Organisation survey finding 87 per cent of farmers uncertain about the industry's future, and said Labor's Farm Finance package funded 17 additional rural financial counsellors while the government withheld $40 million from the low-interest loan scheme.

Supported the dairy levies bill, highlighting Eden-Monaro's Bega Cheese, which employs about 700 people and exports to over 50 countries, and outlined the government's three-stage agriculture white paper process due for completion by the end of 2014.

Supported the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Amendment (Dairy Produce) Bill 2014, noting Western Australia produces less than four per cent of the nation's dairy output at about 340 million litres a year, down from around 400 million litres a decade ago, and explained the bill raises the maximum Animal Health Council levy caps without increasing the actual rate paid by farmers.

Supported the bill, describing Wannon in south-west Victoria as the nation's largest dairy producing area with major processors including Fonterra and Murray Goulburn, recounted the takeover battle for Warrnambool Cheese and Butter won by Canadian company Saputo after its share price doubled, and criticised the opposition's amendment while noting individual dairy farmers pay $7,000 to $15,000 a year in carbon tax costs.

Explained the bill as a free insurance policy allowing dairy farmers to quickly raise a levy cap only if needed to respond to a disease outbreak, without imposing any immediate cost, and highlighted the Norco dairy co-operative in his Page electorate, founded in 1895, which purchased 152 million litres of milk from 159 members and employs 413 people.

Supported the bill, noting Tasmania produces about 10 per cent of the nation's dairy output from just two per cent of its land mass, highlighted a newly appointed livestock biosecurity officer working with the Tasmanian Farmers and Graziers Association, and said the state's 445 dairy farmers account for 40 per cent of the value of Tasmanian agriculture, with businesses like Pyengana Dairy Company winning the 2013 and 2014 Australian Grand Dairy Champion Award for cheddar cheese.

Supported the bill, citing modelling that a major foot-and-mouth disease outbreak could cost the economy $10.3 billion to $16.7 billion, and detailed the struggles of Queensland's 29 dairy farmers supplying the Rockhampton co-operative at a farm-gate price of about 55 cents a litre, warning a looming 6.5 cent carbon tax diesel impost from 1 July could push more of them out of business.

Supported the dairy levies bill, describing dairy as a $17 billion industry, said average herd sizes have grown from about 85 to around 220 head, and said the number of Australian dairy farms has fallen from 22,000 to 6,500 as the sector consolidated.

Supported the dairy levies bill, said the Korea-Australia Free Trade Agreement gives an immediate duty-free quota for 80 per cent of Australia's cheese exports to Korea but takes up to 20 years to eliminate the 36 per cent tariff on the rest, said Australian farmers receive only 3 per cent of income from government support compared with an OECD average of 20 per cent and 60 per cent in Norway, and said drought led to the loss of half of northern Victoria's dairy farms with water sold at $2,400 a megalitre before herds began recovering.

Supported the dairy levies bill, which allows the Australian Animal Health Council levy's protein rate cap to rise from 13 cents to 35 cents per kilogram, said overseas farm-gate milk prices are up to 25 per cent higher in the European Union and United States and over 40 per cent higher in export-focused New Zealand, and said Commonwealth emergency disease funding is generally repaid by industry within 10 years.
Rose to speak on the dairy levies bill but used the opportunity to update the House on the fire situation in Gippsland.

Supported the dairy levies bill, said the electorate has about 160 dairy farmers, said Western Australian milk supply is down 6.1 million litres this year and 18.7 million litres compared with the second half of 2010, and highlighted the Manning family's five generations of dairy farming in the south-west of the state since 1852.

Supported the dairy levies bill, said Queensland dairy farms have fallen from more than 2,500 to fewer than 500, cited a Queensland Dairyfarmers' Organisation survey finding 87 per cent of farmers uncertain about the industry's future amid a cash cost of production of 55.2 cents a litre against a farm-gate price of 51.3 cents, and said the industry believes prices must rise by at least 12 cents a litre to restore confidence.

Supported a bill raising the maximum Australian Animal Health Council levy on dairy produce from 0.058 to 0.145 cents per kilogram of milk fat, needed as Australia exports 50 per cent of its dairy produce overseas. Said the number of dairy farms in her electorate's Mitta Valley fell by 35 per cent over the past decade even as milk production per farmer rose significantly.

Summed up debate on the dairy levy bill, announcing a second drought assistance package giving farmers access to a further $280 million at four per cent interest, and raising the farm household allowance's on-farm net asset threshold from $1.5 million to $2.55 million. Noted dairy exports to Asia were worth $2.76 billion in 2012-13.
Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Amendment (Dairy Produce) Act 2014
